_doc: Permission ledger — single source of truth for what Bash may auto-run. Read by .claude/scripts/bash_permission_gate.py (PreToolUse) and appended to by .claude/scripts/permission_recorder.py (PostToolUse) when the user grants a prompt. allow_keys: form name -> note. A key selects forms from the gate's closed table (ADR-0015): a tool name selects that tool's inert (read-only) forms; a project form (pytest, mypy, ruff check, python3 install.py, the .claude/scripts CLIs, every git and gh form) needs its exact full key and is a stated act of trust in the repository's own code and config. A key naming no form selects nothing. allow_patterns: regex that selects a form-matching part (the feature-branch git push). ask_words: word rules {tool, all: [[word, ...], ...], note} matched on the resolved command words only (subcommand and verb; a word ending '-' matches as a prefix; an empty all guards the tool itself). ask_patterns + denials: regex on the raw text and every normalized part that always forces a human prompt. A hit on either guard layer always wins over every allow_key, allow_pattern and grant. grants: auto-recorded user approvals — only inert forms are ever recorded; empty on a fresh clone.

allow_patterns.note: feature-branch push (feat/fix/feature/docs/chore/refactor/test) — standing exception per git-workflow/boundaries

ask_patterns.note: bypasses the repo's git hooks — confirm each time
mutating gh api call — network write, confirm (boundaries)
use WebFetch/WebSearch for reads; curl/wget can POST — network write, confirm (boundaries)
mutates repo variables/secrets (flags may sit between noun and verb) — network write, confirm (boundaries)
drops a database — data loss, always confirm
printf -v / test -v evaluate a variable name, and an array subscript in it runs code — confirm

ask_words.note: merge stays human (git-workflow); clean deletes untracked files — confirm
mutates repo variables/secrets — network write, confirm (boundaries)
publishes an image or stores registry credentials — human only (boundaries)
drops a database — data loss, always confirm
cloud or state mutation, costs money — confirm (boundaries)
AWS write (delete/change/create/copy/sync/run/...) — costs money or loses data, confirm (boundaries)
